en: The Scripture on the Dhāraṇī of the Blazing Light of Great Majestic Virtue for the Elimination of Calamities and the Bringing of Auspiciousness, Spoken by the Buddha;
translated by the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa, Special Advancement, Acting Courtier of the Court of State Ceremonial, during the Tang Dynasty.
Translated by the Great One of Vast Wisdom, Amoghavajra, by Imperial Decree. At that time, Śākyamuni Buddha was in the celestial palace of the Śuddhāvāsa deities.
He addressed the assembly of planetary deities who roam the sky—the nine great planets and their attendants.
And to the twenty-eight lunar mansions, the deities of the twelve zodiac signs, and all the assembly of holy beings:
I now proclaim the method for removing calamities and disasters through the *Candragarbha-mahātejas-tejo-dhāraṇī*, as taught by the Tathāgata King Śāla in the past.
If there are kings, ministers, their residences, or their realms that are oppressed by the five planets,
or by Rāhu, comets, meteors, and malevolent stars;
When [the planet] shines upon its natal mansion, its various stellar positions,
or when it approaches the Imperial Throne within the state, the family, or the specific territorial division (*fenye*),
at such a time of encroachment and oppression:
For those who cause various obstacles by either retreating or advancing,
one should simply establish a *maṇḍala* in a pure place and recite this *dhāraṇī* one hundred and eight times, or one thousand times.
Whether for one day, two days, three days, or even up to seven days,
one should adorn the ritual site according to the dharma and wholeheartedly receive, uphold, read, and recite [the text].
All calamities shall be entirely extinguished and unable to cause harm.
Should Venus or Mars enter the Southern Dipper (Nandou),
creating various obstacles and difficulties for the state, the family, or the corresponding astrological division (fenye), [this shall be averted].
In front of a single wrathful image,
draw the form of that Śatru;
recite this dhāraṇī with a fierce voice to empower it.
That calamity shall be immediately removed and transferred onto those who do not obey the king’s commands and who act in rebellion.
The recipient then recites the dhāraṇī, saying:
*Namo samantabuddhānām, apratihate...* (Namo samantabuddhānām, apratihate).
Cche tra ha ta śa sa na nām tadyatha oṃ kha kha khahi khahi hūṃ hūṃ jvala jvala prajvala paṭa.

12. *Svāhā* 23. This dhāraṇī was proclaimed together by all the Tathāgatas.
If there be bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, laymen, or laywomen, [who recite it...]
Those who receive, uphold, read, and recite this dhāraṇī will be able to accomplish eighty thousand kinds of auspicious matters and eliminate eighty thousand kinds of inauspicious matters.
If there are kings, ministers, their retinues, or any of the common people who are afflicted by the five planets,
Rāhu, Ketu, comets, meteors, or malevolent stars and spirits;
The imperial throne will be assailed within the state, the family, and the corresponding celestial divisions;
the palaces and lunar mansions under their jurisdiction will witness calamities and disasters arising in competition.
Either Saturn may press down upon them,
causing them to advance or retreat;
or perhaps an enemy from a previous life seeks to plot their harm.
For those who regard various evils, calamities, verbal disputes, malevolent rites, curses,
and incantations as disasters,
may all sentient beings receive and uphold this according to the Dharma.
All calamities shall be entirely extinguished and unable to cause harm;
misfortunes shall be transformed into blessings, and all shall attain auspiciousness.
I now proclaim that the inconceivable merit of this dhāraṇī is peerless.
"Maintain this in secret; do not proclaim it recklessly.
At that time, the Tathāgata addressed the fourfold assembly:
"If there are regions where peace is not maintained and calamities arise together..."
Please purify the assembly and establish the *maṇḍala* according to the Dharma.
Install the Buddha image, perform the boundary-binding (*sīmābandha*),
and provide offerings of incense, flowers, lamps, and candles according to your means.
It causes all sentient beings to obtain immeasurable merit,
and their calamities are immediately eliminated.
At that time, the Tathāgata, having finished speaking this Dhāraṇī Sūtra, [entered samādhi].
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mañjuśrī,
along with the various śrāvakas and the fourfold assembly, the Great Devas who roam through space,
the various stars and constellations, and the entire host of noble ones [were present].
All, in accordance with the Buddha’s command, prostrated, received and upheld [the teaching], and returned to their respective palaces.
Together with the great assembly of devas, nāgas, and the eight classes of beings,
having heard what the Buddha had spoken, they were all greatly rejoiced, believed, accepted, and practiced it accordingly.
The Sūtra on the Dhāraṇī of the Blazing Radiance, Great Majestic Virtue, for Eliminating Calamities and Bringing Auspiciousness, Spoken by the Buddha.
